items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: He and Cook, those fellas, they had some of the best jobs to be had.

ctx.x: I talked to him the other day.

He had a studio right there at 36th Estate you know. He had the band in Milwaukee, the Wisconsin roof, before Sims had it. He comes or he leaves there and goes to Savoy. That's when Sims goes on in there and when Sims is about a year or so I go in there with Sims. But he had a good band, he had a good band, he had good Harmon's Bremen. He had Riverview. He and Cook, those fellas, they had some of the best jobs to be had. McGuire's down on Clark Street. I follow Roy and Dutray and him all around. And I get into…
Yeah, he's from Denver but he's been there.
Well, as you grew on in years, did you hear any more music?

Oh yeah, I, in spite of me hearing this music, I used to say, the second line just like the rest of the kids. We used to try sometime way away from home, you know, out of the neighborhood. I remember I, I think it was about the 30th of May and some friends of mine and I, we, we came all the way down to French Bar Town and the boys got behind us and ran us all the way to the podgers and ramparts, you know. And so I always did love music. I used to do a lot of whistling. I still do. And so, but I didn't have no…
Where was he from? He's from New Orleans.
